rows.description: A wise person separates what can be influenced from what cannot, plans for what is possible and lets go of the rest. Tolerating not knowing is a skill that grows with practice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague or partner under constant checking feels distrusted and stops using their own judgment. Naming the impact calmly and agreeing on clear check-in points restores balance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A team sees a manager who cannot let go of details and decides everything. Productivity suffers and people learn helplessness; feedback framed around results rather than personality is likelier to be heard.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child believes practice, effort and choices shape outcomes, and tries again after losing. This helps learning, but it can turn into blaming self for things beyond their control.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: External: it just happens to me [Actor]
rows.description: A child blames luck, teachers or the test for every result and feels there is little use in trying. Often learned from repeated experiences of not being heard, and small wins that show impact rebuild belief.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager from a traditional home believes in destiny and also studies hard, holding both without contradiction. Cultural belief in fate can bring peace after loss without removing personal responsibility.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A wise teenager asks what is within their control today and takes one action on it. Pairing effort with acceptance of what cannot be changed keeps hope without self-blame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult who believes everything is their fault takes on guilt for others' choices, while another blames everyone else and never changes. Both distort; balanced view separates own part from circumstances.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague notices a peer who has stopped suggesting ideas after being ignored many times. Recognising that the passivity was learned, not laziness, opens the way to restore agency with small real choices.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Honesty versus loyalty to a friend [Actor]
rows.description: A child sees a best friend cheat and feels torn between telling and staying loyal. Both feel like good values, and the child needs adults who help think it through rather than shame either choice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
